title: Make-Up Tips: Which Eyeliner Is Best For Your Skin Tone And Type?
text:
Make-Up Tips: Which Eyeliner Is Best For Your Skin Tone And Type?
Choosing the right eyeliner isn’t just about colour, it depends on your skin tone and type. From fair to dark skin, oily to dry, here’s how to find your perfect match
Applying eyeliner may seem simple, but it is an art form. While many women use eyeliner daily, a surprising number do not realise that choosing the right one depends greatly on their skin tone and type. Most often, people stick to classic black or brown shades, but your perfect eyeliner shade might be something entirely different.
Fair Skin

People with fair skin can pull off almost any eyeliner colour. However, soft shades like grey and light brown enhance their features beautifully. For a more vibrant look, shades like blue, green, or light purple work wonders.
Medium/Wheatish Skin Tone
Black eyeliner gives a bold, striking effect to those with a wheatish complexion, adding an attractive glow to the face. Bronze, burgundy, and plum shades also suit this skin tone well. For a more natural look, opt for dark grey or brown liners. If it’s a party look you’re aiming for, golden or copper-toned eyeliners are perfect.
Dark Skin Tone
Those with darker complexions should explore bold and bright shades. Deep plum, cobalt blue, and orange can bring out their features beautifully. For a glamorous touch, gold, bronze, and copper liners are great choices. Emerald green is another standout shade. You can also try white or silver eyeliner on the waterline to make your eyes appear bigger and brighter. Always finish off with mascara to complete the look.
Consider Your Skin Type Too
Beyond skin tone, your skin type also plays a big role in choosing the right eyeliner. Picking a formula that suits your skin ensures your liner lasts longer and doesn’t smudge.
Oily Skin: Oily skin, especially during humid weather, can cause makeup to melt or smudge easily. Go for waterproof or gel-based eyeliners. Pencil eyeliners are also a good option. Always use a primer on the eyelids to create a smooth base, this helps the liner stay intact all day.
Dry Skin: Those with dry skin should stick to creamy and hydrating products. Use eyeliner with moisturising properties, cream-based formulas work best and glide on smoothly.
Combination Skin: If you have combination skin, you’re in luck. You can experiment with all types of eyeliners—liquid, pencil, or gel. After application, you can set it with a matching eyeshadow to lock it in.
Sensitive Skin: For those with sensitive skin prone to rashes or irritation, always choose hypoallergenic, dermatologist-tested eyeliners. Avoid products with strong fragrances or harsh chemicals.
